keyRules: Mandatory registration with IDAC via Vuela Seguro: RAD 48 (amendment in force since 21/02/2025) requires it from 0.20 kg (0.44 lb); the Vuela Seguro guide still states 0.25 kg (0.55 lb) — confirm with IDAC if your drone weighs 200–249 g
Drones >250 g (0.55 lb): IDAC remote pilot license or certificate required, also for recreational use (min. 18 years, RAD 107.23)

Recreational flights: IDAC (Vuela Seguro guide) requires a permit application using form 1500-9 (license/certificate, registration, insurance if applicable and map with coordinates) at least 5 business days before the operation; estimated processing time 15 business days
Minimum distance of 9 km (5 nautical miles) from airports and airfields without IDAC authorization.
Outside class G airspace (e.g. airport control zones), prior IDAC authorization and coordination with ATC are required (RAD 107.57)
Flying is permitted only during the day—night flying requires a specific IDAC permit
Always keep the drone within direct line of sight (VLOS)
Maximum height 400 ft (122 m) above ground level (RAD 107.67); flying over uninvolved people is prohibited without prior IDAC authorization (RAD 107.55)
Flying from a moving vehicle or vessel is prohibited without IDAC authorization, except over sparsely populated areas (RAD 107.39)

MANDATORY third-party liability insurance (RAD 48.19 and RAD 107.69; for recreational use between 0.25 and 2 kg, RAD 107.69 accepts a Sworn Declaration of Joint and Several Liability (Declaración Jurada de Responsabilidad Solidaria))
Drones >2 kg (4.4 lb): liability insurance required also for recreational use (min. USD 2,000, RAD 107.69; RAD 48.19 requires min. USD 5,000 above 4.5 kg)
Flying over is PROHIBITED: National Palace, Ministry of Defense, San Isidro Air Base
Flying over is PROHIBITED: Dominican Oil Refinery, Las Calderas Naval Base, military command posts
Commercial operation: IDAC remote pilot license + permit (form 1500-9). Foreign nationals: only if hired by a Dominican company
Do not interfere with air traffic in aerodrome landing/takeoff patterns
importantNotes: 📋 LEGAL FRAMEWORK: Drone operations are regulated by Civil Aviation Law 491-06 + RAD-107 (small unmanned aircraft system) + RAD-48 (registration and labeling). The IDAC (Dominican Civil Aviation Institute) is the competent authority.

✈️ FOREIGN TOURISTS: These rules apply to non-residents. Before flying, apply for a permit from IDAC using form 1500-9 (min. 5 business days in advance; estimated processing time 15 business days), attaching your license/certificate, registration, insurance if applicable and a map with coordinates. If your country does not require a license/registration because of the drone's weight, attach that part of your national regulations and a copy of your ID. Registration: RAD 48 requires it from 0.20 kg (the Vuela Seguro guide states 0.25 kg); for drones of 200–249 g (e.g. DJI Mini, Flip), confirm with IDAC. Even if registration is not required, all other rules apply. Commercial use: only if you are hired by a Dominican company that applies for it.

🏖️ PUNTA CANA AND COASTAL TOURIST AREAS: The airports PUJ (Punta Cana), SDQ (Las Américas), and STI (Santiago) have a 9 km exclusion zone. Saona, Catalina, Bayahibe, Las Galeras: Many beaches and resorts have additional restrictions—check with your hotel or tour operator before flying.

🌳 PROTECTED AREAS: Before flying in national parks (Los Haitises, del Este/Saona, Sierra de Bahoruco, Jaragua, Lago Enriquillo), check with the Ministry of the Environment; authorization may be required. Respect wildlife — whales in Samaná (Jan–Mar).

🏛️ PROHIBITED AND RESTRICTED ZONES: IDAC includes, among others, the National Palace, the Presidential Residence, the Ministry of Defense, San Isidro Air Base, the 27 de Febrero and Las Calderas naval bases, the Dominican Oil Refinery and Loma de Alto Bandera. Do not fly in them without IDAC permission (RAD 107.61). Check NOTAMs for temporary restrictions.

fields.disclaimerText: Always check IDAC’s official sources before flying. This app is a tool, not a legal authority. The Dominican Republic enforces Civil Aviation Law 491-06 along with Regulations RAD-107 (sUAS operations) and RAD-48 (registration). The official website is Vuela Seguro (idac.gob.do/drone).
